items.title: AI Boom Faces a Growing Public Backlash
items.content: <article>The Atlantic CEO Nicholas Thompson tells Bloomberg This Weekend that AI offers powerful tools for businesses but poses significant risks to media, while its broader economic impact continues to lag behind rapidly advancing capabilities. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Thompson also discusses the discipline of distance running and how the sport shaped his relationship with his father and became an organizing force in his life.  (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: AI Boom Brings New Business to Matchmakers
items.content: <article>Linx Dating founder and CEO Amy Andersen tells Bloomberg This Weekend that newly wealthy AI creators are fueling demand for high-end matchmaking as busy professionals seek an alternative to dating apps. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Andersen explains how her firm vets and recruits potential partners for selective clients, with matchmaking packages that can exceed $500,000. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Making Advanced MicroChips Takes a Global Ecosystem
items.content: <article>On Bloomberg This Weekend, Gideon Lewis-Kraus explains how advanced chipmaking depends on a deeply interconnected global network of specialized companies, including ASML and TSMC, making semiconductor supply chains extraordinarily difficult to replicate or relocate. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Lewis-Kraus describes the remarkable engineering behind ASML’s EUV machines and why rebuilding a semiconductor ecosystem in the US is a generational project rather than a simple exercise in reshoring. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Technical Colleges Bet on AI-Driven Demand for Skilled Workers
items.author: Rachel Phua
items.content: <article>Technical colleges are betting a surge in demand for skilled workers will lift profits, though the payoff may take time as they expand campuses and programs to accommodate more students.</article>

items.title: Bank of Israel Slams Netanyahu’s Anti-Sanctions Crypto Proposal
items.author: Galit Altstein
items.content: <article>Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu floated using cryptocurrency to get around potential financial sanctions on Israel, prompting a strongly-worded rebuke from the central bank.</article>

items.title: Secretive Ukrainian Unit Behind Rapid Expansion of Deep-Strike Campaign
items.author: Kollen Post
items.content: <article>When he started flying unmanned aircraft in combat, “Ray” was flying some of Ukraine’s earliest mid-range strike drones, on missions of about 100 kilometers with a warhead about the weight of a bowling ball.</article>

items.title: Japan’s GMO Internet Requests Government Cyber Defense Measures
items.author: Taiga Uranaka
items.content: <article>Japanese IT services provider GMO Internet Group Inc. said it has asked the government to deploy active cyber defense as the company works to contain the fallout from a hacking incident.</article>

items.title: Malaysia May Widen Ban on Israel-Based Waze Traffic App, PM Says
items.author: Anuradha Raghu
items.content: <article>Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said Malaysia’s security cannot be compromised as he held fast on the government’s partial ban of Google’s navigation app Waze and said authorities aren’t ruling out even wider restrictions.</article>

items.title: UK Vows £100 Million for Biosecurity Lab With OpenAI, Anthropic
items.author: Jacob Reid
items.content: <article>The UK announced £100 million ($134 million) for a AI Biosecurity Lab which will be supported by OpenAI, Anthropic and Google DeepMind, part of a raft of measures designed to improve the government’s ability to understand and tackle the risks posed by the technology.</article>

items.title: $1,999 New iPhone 'Unfolds' During Affordability Crisis
items.content: <article>Bloomberg's Lisa Mateo, Scarlet Fu, and Tom Keene discuss the release of the new Apple iPhone on this weeks edition of "Bloomberg Money." (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: The Points Guy CEO: People Are Leveraging Loyalty
items.content: <article>Brian Kelly discusses findings from The Points Guy’s State of Loyalty report, saying its focus is on where consumer trust and loyalty are growing—not simply whether people are loyal overall. Fuel and dining programs posted 88% consumer satisfaction, which Kelly links to rising everyday costs: consumers are using rewards for immediate savings while wages stagnate and expenses climb. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: AI Jitters, Oil & Big Tech
items.content: <article>The Close brings you the latest news and analysis leading up to the final minutes and seconds before and after the closing bell on Wall Street. Today's guests are BlackRock Deputy CIO, Global Fixed Income Russ Brownback, AXA Group Chief Economist Gilles Moëc, Mizuho Securities Senior Equity Research Analyst Lloyd Walmsley, AlixPartners Co-CEO Rob Hornby, Interactive Brokers Chief Strategist Steve Sosnick, Teneo CoiPresident, Political Risk Advisory Kevin Kajiwara, KPMG US Principal, Consumer & Retail Strategy Julia Wilson, The Points Guy Founder & CEO Brian Kelly, & Green Bay Packers Former Vice President Andrew Brandt. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Consumers to Ramp up Holiday Spending This Year: KPMG
items.content: <article>Julia Wilson, Principal of Consumer and Retail Strategy at KPMG US, discusses the firm’s holiday survey, which projects spending will increase 5% year over year. She says much of the rise reflects higher prices, though consumers are still willing to spend on priorities. She speaks to Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Investors Figuring Out Agentic AI: Robinhood's Guild
items.content: <article>Stephanie Guild, CIO of Robinhood, joins Scarlet Fu and Tom Keene on "Bloomberg Money." They discuss how she is seeing consumers take advantage of the pullback in AI, having cash on the side to invest, and how Robinhood users can now use agentic AI agents to invest on their behalf.  (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: AlixPartners Co-CEO Rob Hornby on AI Bull Case
items.content: <article>Rob Hornby says AI costs are falling faster than those of comparable technologies historically, but remain substantial. He describes companies as being in a transition period: investment is underway while returns are uneven, and the shift from flat fees to per-token charges has exposed costs. He speaks with Romaine Bostick & Jess Menton on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: The Urgent Need for Whistleblowers
items.content: <article>“You Can See Everything” is the latest reminder of how whistleblowers are more important than ever. But at the same time the role is becoming more complicated — and opaque, Bloomberg Opinion columnist Beth Kowitt says. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: AI Ushers in New Era of Cybersecurity Needs
items.content: <article>The US government is working to address and stop any potential cybersecurity issues stemming from flaws in PHP, a widely used open-source software, that may impact federal agencies and American critical infrastructure, according to a White House official.  The programming language, called PHP, contains two vulnerabilities which could potentially expose organizations using it in websites and software platforms to cyberattacks.  Jay Chaudhry, CEO & Founder, Zscaler says we need new more proactive measures beyond firewalls.  (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Instacart Considers a Potential Sale, Sparking Share Rally
items.author: Mark Gurman
items.content: <article>Instacart has explored a potential sale of the grocery-delivery company, a process that has included discussions with Uber Technologies Inc., a person familiar with the matter said.</article>

items.title: OpenAI Resumes Training AI, But Without Internet Access
items.author: Rachel Metz
items.content: <article>OpenAI has begun cutting off internet access for its most capable artificial intelligence models during the training process in response to prior incidents in which its systems breached other companies.</article>

items.title: Apple’s iPhone Duo Hits Stores in Face of Short Supply and High Demand
items.author: Bloomberg News
items.content: <article>Apple Inc. quickly sold out of its limited in-store inventory for the new iPhone Duo, underscoring the strong demand for a foldable device that starts at nearly $2,000.</article>
